items.title: Add an optional TensorAtomic placement for MCore MFSDP v2 dense parameters
items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back. This PR adds an optional alternative: with `MFSDP_TENSOR_ATOMIC=1`, every dense parameter stays whole on one owner rank (the `TensorAtomic` placement), so the Muon step needs no gather or scatter. Owners are chosen greedily to balance the Newton-Schulz cost. The plan depends only on parameter shapes, so every rank computes the same one. Experts keep their own mesh.

items.author: shiv4289
items.summary: Fixes undercounting of preemptions in vLLM metrics by moving the counter from the frontend resume event to the scheduler, ensuring aborted-preempted requests are captured at the correct time.
items.body:
## Overview

`vllm:num_preemptions` is counted from the request's `PREEMPTED` event, which only reaches the frontend with that request's next output. So a request that is preempted and then aborted before it resumes is never counted, and the rest are counted late. This counts preemptions in the scheduler and reports them in `SchedulerStats`, like the prefix cache stats.

## Claims

- Requests aborted while preempted are counted.
- The counter moves when the preemption happens, not when the request resumes.
- `vllm:request_num_preemptions` and `IterationStats.num_preempted_reqs` are unchanged

items.body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #48076 (the UniBoost policy). The right `gamma` depends on the load: it sets how far a short request may jump a long one, and a fixed value is either too timid at low load or starves large requests under overload. The paper's gamma-Ada estimator (Eq. 9) tracks it online from the response-time tail: `gamma_hat = ln(5) / (t99 - t95)`. This PR adds it as `--uniboost-adaptive-gamma`.

## Motivation

With attention DP and TP MoE on CUDA, the MoE input of a decode step is a MAX_LEN gather: every DP rank contributes a slot of the same length, and the rows past its real requests are padding. The router sends the padding rows to experts like real tokens, so every MoE layer loads those experts' weights.

items.author: dilberx
items.summary: Fixes Rust vllm-bench backends to correctly fail streams that terminate early without [DONE], contain error objects, or produce no tokens.
items.body:
The `openai` and `openai-chat` backends in the Rust `vllm-bench` count an HTTP 200 stream as successful no matter how it ends:

- `[DONE]` is skipped, so a stream that closes early, even after the usage chunk, still succeeds.
- In-stream error objects (`{"error": {...}}` or a flat `{"object": "error", ...}`) are not detected.
- `openai-chat` sets `success = true` even when no token arrived. `openai` already required one.

## Motivation

With `--allow-auto-truncate`, `_validate_one_request` cuts an over-long input to exactly `context_len`. The total-token check right below then sees `input + max_new_tokens > context_len` and clamps `max_new_tokens` to 0, so the request returns no output, the opposite of what enabling auto-truncate asks for.

The same branch also drops `num_reserved_tokens` (the output slots EAGLE reserves) from `input_token_num` after truncating, although the check above it had counted them. With EAGLE a truncated request therefore ends `num_reserved_tokens` past the context.

Fixes #7829

When using block-scoped CUDA graphs with pipeline parallelism, each forward pass allocated a new recv buffer tensor via torch.empty(). The CUDA graph captured the buffer address read through HybridStack.input_tensor (a Python attribute set via set_input_tensor()). items.body:
## Motivation

HiCache storage backends only see the L3 traffic they serve. Prefix hits served from device or host memory never reach storage, so a backend cannot tell that a stored prefix is still hot, and a backend that offers a minimum retention time (e.g. to back a prompt-cache TTL) has no way to receive the per-request TTL.

## Modifications

- `HiCacheStorage.batch_touch(keys, extra_info=None)`: new optional hook, **default no-op**. Called once per finished request with the request's whole page-hash chain (from the sequence start), so a backend can renew retention of pages served from me

## Overview


Measured workload requests currently retry connection reset, refused, and
timeout failures up to three times. A later successful attempt can hide an
overloaded or unstable service and report the sample as successful.

The retry also changes the workload being measured: failed attempts and
backoff are omitted from per-request latency, while they still extend the
overall benchmark duration and retain a concurrency slot. This can produce
normal-looking latency and failure counts alongside unexpectedly lower
throughput.

Remove automatic retries only from the measured request path

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.body:
## Description

`setup.py` now hard-links the package files when it builds the wheel, instead of letting setuptools copy them. The wheel is the same. The build is faster and puts less load on the filesystem metadata server.

Before this PR, `python -m build --wheel` copied the whole package twice before it zipped it. `build_py` copied `tensorrt_llm/` and the other packages into `build/lib.<platform>/`. Then `install_lib` copied `build/lib.<platform>/` into `build/bdist.<platform>/wheel/`, which `bdist_wheel` zips and then deletes. For a built checkout that is 2.4 GB in 13,207 files, each time.

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Decode each streaming-input chunk after its own prompt
items.author: paolo-perrone
items.summary: With streaming input, the frontend detokenizer only ever sees the first chunk's prompt. Each later chunk's output gets decoded straight after the previous chunk's output, so when a chunk stops partway through a character (maxtokens landing on a byte token), th…
items.body:
## Overview

With streaming input, the frontend detokenizer only ever sees the first chunk's prompt. Each later chunk's output gets decoded straight after the previous chunk's output, so when a chunk stops partway through a character (max_tokens landing on a byte token), the next chunk's text starts with U+FFFD. This PR feeds each new chunk's prompt to the detokenizer as context, the same way the scheduler builds the model's context.

## Claims

- After a chunk that ends partway through a multi-byte character, the next chunk's text no longer starts with U+FFFD. That holds for DELTA and CUMUL

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash NVIDIA support is in `main` ([#45925](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45925) and follow-ups), so the cookbook no longer needs the "install from the support PR (TBD)" step or the one-off `dev-minimax-m31-flash` image everywhere.

The latest release, v0.5.23, includes #45925. items.title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Skip the redundant output copy in MoRI finalize
items.author: davzhuAMD
items.summary: copies the first rows of MoRI's combine output into the modular kernel's tensor. This PR returns that slice instead, so each MoE layer launches one fewer copy kernel on the MoRI EP path. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

`MoriPrepareAndFinalize.finalize` copies the first `num_tokens` rows of MoRI's combine output into the modular kernel's `output` tensor (`output.copy_(result[:num_token])`). This PR returns that slice instead, so each MoE layer launches one fewer copy kernel on the MoRI EP path. Within a forward pass, outputs are bit-identical.

Related:
- #44452 (closed, never merged) proposed this for every backend.

## Motivation

items.summary: Fixes catastrophic cancellation in speculative-decoding acceptance estimator where high-confidence drafts lose signal in fp32, replacing 11.5% of values with a constant.
items.body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #52228, which added the estimator to do adaptive verification without a confidence head.

The adaptive-verification acceptance feature loses its entire signal to catastrophic cancellation whenever the drafter is confident. Every draft row more confident than `1 - 6e-8` reports the same acceptance feature, `40.0`, whatever its true confidence is. The feature is specified as a log-odds, `logit(q(m*))`, but it recovers the complement mass by subtracting 1 from a sum that includes the max's own unit term, which in fp32 destroys the quantity being measured — no NaN

items.author: Pb314314
items.summary: Encoder CUDA graphs only save eager's host launch time. On main they are also captured and replayed where eager is GPU-bound, and a batch can be split into several padded replays.
items.body:
## Overview

Encoder CUDA graphs only save eager's host launch time. On main they are also captured and replayed where eager is GPU-bound, and a batch can be split into several padded replays. On those batches the graph is slower than eager: up to 2.7x on MiniMax-M3 and 1.7x on DeepSeek-V4.1. This PR replays each batch at most once, and captures only the budgets whose replay beats eager. Everything larger runs as one eager forward. The capture budgets are now chosen by measurement rather than by `max_num_batched_tokens`.

items.title: [RFC]: TokenGate integration into vLLM
items.author: luis-gasparschroeder
items.summary: Proposes integrating TokenGate learned token pruning into vLLM for Qwen3/Qwen3.5, selectively dropping prefill tokens to reduce TTFT and KV-cache memory.
items.body:
### Motivation.

I’m working on integrating [TokenGate](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26754) into vLLM, starting with Qwen3 and Qwen3.5. 

TokenGate adapts pretrained language models to perform learned token pruning during prefill. A trained gate scores the prunable input tokens at an intermediate layer and selects a subset to retain, alongside all non-prunable tokens. Subsequent layers process this shorter sequence, reducing prefill computation and KV-cache storage in the full-attention layers above the gate.

We evaluated Qwen3-1.7B on RepoBench-P, 2WikiMultihopQA, MultiNews, BioDEX, and needle

## Motivation

Two Triton kernels used by Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next compute token offsets from an int32 `tl.program_id(0)`. items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Makes Rust server idle scheduling match Python server: only park on request ring when --sleep-on-idle is set, reducing low-load latency.

With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, the scheduler rank that hosts the Rust listener always installs `RustServerIdleSleeper`, so between requests its idle loop parks for up to 1 s on the in-process request ring. ## Purpose

Granite 4.2 emits tool calls in an XML format:

```
<tool_call>

vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b \

    --enable-auto-tool-choice

`GraniteToolCallParser` is a thin subclass of the existing `GraniteThinkingParser`

items.body:
## Overview

When a streamed `/v1/responses` request fails during generation, the server's error handler raises instead of telling the client, so the SSE stream just stops. This sends an `error` event and ends the stream cleanly.

## Claims

- A streamed Responses request that fails mid-generation now ends with an `error` event. Its `code` is the HTTP status of the failure: `"500"`, or `"503"` when the request can be retried.
- The handler no longer throws a pydantic `ValidationError` out of the stream generator.
- Non-streaming Responses, Chat Completions and Completions aren't changed.

items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #64327. Unblocks #63801.

FlashInfer's MNNVL fused all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm has a cluster-barrier race (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7782). The vLLM default single-node backend has been MNNVL since #61989. With HiSparse running host-memory gathers on its copy stream, the race fires and the engine dies with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` (Xid 13 `CTA Not Present`).

With HiSparse enabled and `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=auto`, backend selection now:
- single node: uses `trtllm`;
- multi-node: disables FlashInfer all-reduce, since `trtllm` doesn't support mul

items.body:
## Description

On the disaggregated server, a streamed `/v1/responses` request receives no bytes at all, not even the HTTP status line, until the context phase is done. The route awaits the pipeline before it creates the `StreamingResponse`, and the pipeline returns its stream only once the context worker has answered: in context-first order that is the context POST, which never streams, and in generation-first order the pipeline also waits for the context response before it returns the generation stream. Queueing plus prefill of a long agent prompt takes tens of seconds to minutes under load

Add a fused kernel path for wide-residual hybrid models with shortcut- connected MoE (--wide-residual-shortcut-moe-kernel-fusion). ## Motivation

`DefaultModelLoader` filters MTP checkpoint weights when `draft_model_idx` is set (`_filter_mtp_weights` in `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py`): it keeps only the requested MTP layer, remaps it to layer 0, preserves non-MTP weights, and yields lazily so the upstream buffered iterator's sliding window bounds CPU memory. Equal ring sizes do not prevent the failure.

## Overview

`KimiVLConfig` passed `pad_token_id` to `super().__init__` as a keyword argument. With the dataclass-based `PreTrainedConfig`, `pad_token_id` is not a declared field.

items.title: [Fix] unified-cache: Skip re-offloading pages restored from the external linker
items.author: AMD-yanfeiwang
items.summary: With the unified cache external linker, a request that restores a prefix from the store uploads that prefix again. writes the restored tail into request-private slots.
items.body:
## Motivation

With the unified cache external linker, a request that restores a prefix from the store uploads that prefix again. `load_back` writes the restored tail into request-private slots. After the forward, the request inserts the tail into the tree as new nodes with `external_cache_stored=False`. Because the linker sets `write_through_threshold=1`, those nodes are backed up again right away.

Mooncake hides this: `batch_set_v2` filters out keys that already exist before writing. `UMBPDirectLinker` has no such filter, so every turn writes the whole restored prefix to the store again.

## Overview

`EmbeddingRequest` is a five-member pydantic union with no discriminator, so every `/v1/embeddings` body is validated against all five. The chat-input members (#45173) check each input item against every chat message type, so a 256×64 token-id batch spends ~66 ms in validation on the API server's event loop. This tries `EmbeddingCompletionRequest` first when `input` is not chat-shaped and the body has no chat-only field, and otherwise (or on any error) falls back to the original union.

## Claims

- Validation of plain inputs: 256×64 token ids ~66 ms → 0.28 ms, 256 strings 818 →

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Stop accepting gRPC connections when shutdown starts
items.author: theminjunchoi
items.summary: Fixes #65155 along with #65156. tonic holds on to the listener passed to until every connection has drained. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #65155 along with #65156. tonic holds on to the listener passed to `serve_with_incoming_shutdown` until every connection has drained. So if a gRPC call was still open during a `--shutdown-timeout` drain, new gRPC clients could still connect but never got a response. Now the incoming stream drops the listener as soon as shutdown starts, like the HTTP server already does, and tonic still drains the open connections.

## Claims

- After shutdown starts, new gRPC connections are refused, even while other gRPC calls are running.
- Calls that are already open still finish.

Part of #65155. The parent process kept its copies of the HTTP and gRPC sockets after passing them to the Rust frontend, so both ports kept listening after Rust closed its listeners at shutdown. items.title: [Bugfix][XPU] Make layer_norm batch invariant under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
items.author: tzielinski-habana
items.summary: Fixes non-deterministic layer_norm behavior on Intel XPU under batch invariance mode by registering a per-row Triton kernel to bypass XPU's row-count-dependent reduction path.
items.body:
## Purpose

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `test_batch_invariance_vlm.py` (Qwen3-VL-2B) fails on XPU: 3 of 4 requests give different logprobs at batch 1 vs batch N.

Root cause: on XPU (torch 2.14.0+xpu), native `layer_norm` uses a different reduction once a call has >= 256 rows. Rows then differ from the same rows normalized in a small batch (hidden 1024-4096, bf16/fp16/fp32, max diff 3e-5 to 1e-3). The vision encoder calls it on all patches of the batch. `enable_batch_invariant_mode()` overrides GEMMs on XPU but not `layer_norm`.

This PR registers a per-row Triton `aten::native_layer_norm`

items.title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Count NaNs in logits per request, not per logits row
items.author: DemisEom
items.summary: Fixes MRV2 NaN counting in logits to aggregate per-request instead of per-logits-row, correcting misattribution during speculative decoding.
items.body:
## Overview

With Model Runner V2, `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` / `VLLM_RAISE_ON_LOGIT_NANS` attribute NaN counts to the wrong requests whenever a request has more than one logits row (speculative decoding, or `num_new_sampled_tokens_per_step > 1`). `get_num_nans` counts NaNs per logits row and `AsyncOutput` zips that array with `req_ids`, so request `j` gets row `j`'s count and rows past `num_reqs` are dropped. This PR makes `get_num_nans` return one count per request.

items.title: Add flattened bucket broadcasting for weight updates
items.author: sheep0923
items.summary: This PR adds --update-weight-broadcast-mode to control how full weights are broadcast to rollout engines: - per-param (default): broadcasts each parameter separately. The flattened mode preserves mixed tensor dtypes and passes loadformat="flattenedbucket" to S…
items.body:
This PR adds --update-weight-broadcast-mode to control how full weights are broadcast to rollout engines:
- per-param (default): broadcasts each parameter separately.
- flattened-bucket: packs each update bucket into a single byte tensor and broadcasts it once, reducing collective calls.
The flattened mode preserves mixed tensor dtypes and passes load_format="flattened_bucket" to SGLang for reconstruction and loading. The configuration is also forwarded through the tensor updater’s distributed path.

Flattened broadcasting requires --update-weight-mode=full, --update-weight-transport=nccl

items.summary: Disables SO_REUSEPORT for the vLLM gRPC server so a second instance on an occupied port fails with Address already in use instead of silently sharing traffic.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #65141. gRPC Core enables `SO_REUSEPORT` by default, so a second `vllm serve --grpc` on a busy port starts up and takes part of the first server's traffic. This sets `grpc.so_reuseport` to 0, like #47529 did for the HTTP server and the Rust frontend.

## Claims

- Starting a second gRPC server on a port that's in use now fails with "Address already in use".
- A single server behaves the same as before.

## Validation

I ran two servers on port 50051 with different `--served-model-name`s (main's `grpc_server.py` on the `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest` image, `facebook/opt-125m`)

items.author: ZhengGong-amd
items.summary: At decode batch sizes the gfx950 MXFP8 dense GEMM launches only workgroups (20 for MiniMax-M3 TP8 qkv on a 256-CU MI355X), each walking all of K, so this PR splits K across extra programs when that grid underfills the CUs and K is long, then reduces the fp32 p…
items.body:
## Motivation

At decode batch sizes the gfx950 MXFP8 `dot_scaled` dense GEMM launches only `cdiv(M, 64) * cdiv(N, BLOCK_N)` workgroups (20 for MiniMax-M3 TP8 qkv on a 256-CU MI355X), each walking all of K, so this PR splits K across extra programs when that grid underfills the CUs and K is long, then reduces the fp32 partials.

This kernel is the default dense path for MXFP8 checkpoints on gfx950. With the MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 MI355X cookbook recipe (TP8, `--quantization mxfp8`), qkv (1280x6144) and the dense-layer gate_up (3072x6144) split; o_proj and dense down (K = 1024 / 1536) are unchanged.

## Motivation

The non-MLA NHD batch-prefill path in the aiter backend copies the whole of q on every layer (`q.contiguous().view(...)`) although `mha_batch_prefill_func` does not need it to be contiguous; splitting q into heads as a view removes that copy. items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Keep same-host NIXL on NVLink with the extensible KV cache
items.author: gcanlin
items.summary: Fixes same-host NIXL KV transfers falling back to TCP instead of NVLink after the extensible KV cache became default, restoring zero-copy cuda_ipc transport and reducing transfer time from 9.9s to ~24ms.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Since the extensible KV cache (#56492) became the default, same-host NIXL P/D silently moves KV over TCP instead of NVLink. This keeps NVLink: with an IMEX channel the cache gets a FABRIC handle, and without one it stays off for NIXL by default.

## Claims

- Per KV transfer, same-host: **9.9 s → about 24 ms**.
- With an IMEX channel, NVLink and the extensible KV cache work together.
- Nothing changes without NIXL on device memory.

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash 1P1D on one node, DEP4 + DEP4, 8x B200, driver 590.48.01, NIXL 1.5.2, real MTP 5, 1,319 GS

items.title: [Bugfix] shm_broadcast: unblock writer in acquire_write when shutdown
items.author: Absoler
items.summary: When a writer is blocked in (e.g., due to a dead reader), won't help because never check. This pr add this check, so allowing to unblock writers symmetrically with readers. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

Fix #65135 . When a writer is blocked in `acquire_write` (e.g., due to a dead reader), `shutdown` won't help because `acquire_write` never check `self.shutting_down`. This pr add this check, so allowing `shutdown` to unblock writers symmetrically with readers.

`shutdown` is already invoked on writer-side queues in serveral places, such as "MultiprocExecutor.shutdown", " WorkerProc.shutdown", "WorkerProc.monitor_death_pipe". The docstring limitation to idle readers is updated accordingly.

## Claims

- Fix a bug where `MessageQueue.shutdown()` had no effect on writers

## Overview

Load unquantized DeepSeek V4.1 BF16 Engram tables without requiring FP8 scale tensors. Preserve checkpoint precision in GPU and CPU-offloaded lookups while retaining the existing FP8 path.

- BF16 SFT checkpoints without quantization metadata load Engram rows as BF16, without `weight_scale_inv` checkpoint parameters or silent casts to FP8.
- BF16 lookup works with GPU, pinned-host, huge-page and DP-shared storage, including uneven TP/DP head shards and CUDA graph replay.
- Existing FP8 scale decoding and packed lookup remain covered by the Engram regression suites.

items.author: wirsbf
items.summary: The vLLM Python gRPC server silently ignores configured API keys instead of enforcing authentication; this PR rejects startup with ValueError when an API key is provided.
items.body:
## Overview

`vllm serve --grpc` accepts `--api-key` / `VLLM_API_KEY` but never enforces them: the Python gRPC server has no authentication, so a configured key is silently ignored and every RPC is anonymous. This PR makes it fail at startup instead, as the vLLM security team suggested.

## Claims

- The Python gRPC server refuses to start when an API key is configured through `--api-key`, `api_key` in `--config`, or `VLLM_API_KEY`. This covers every way to launch it: `vllm serve --grpc`, `python -m vllm.entrypoints.launchers.grpc_server`, the deprecated `vllm.entrypoints.grpc_server`, and smg

items.body:
## Overview

NIXL pairs every KV cache group's blocks at one P/D block size ratio, which comes from the lcm of the groups' block sizes. If one group's own P/D ratio differs, that group's KV lands at the wrong tokens without an error. This PR adds the groups' block sizes to the handshake metadata and rejects such peers at the handshake.

## Claims

- A P/D pair whose KV cache groups' block sizes don't all change by the same ratio fails the handshake with `NotImplementedError`, in pull and push. Before, Mamba hybrids passed the handshake. The transfer then put that group's KV at the wrong tokens

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

items.title: Enter the paged-stash capacity reduction on every rank
items.author: Connor-XY
items.summary: Fixes deadlock in PagedStashRunner.check_moe_overflow where non-MoE pipeline stages skip an all_reduce collective, causing hangs during MoE over-budget reruns.
items.body:
**Why.** `PagedStashRunner.check_moe_overflow` first votes over WORLD on whether any rank went over its receive budget. When one did, a second `all_reduce` takes the MAX of the receive capacity the step needed. Only ranks whose model chunks hold an MoE layer that reports a required capacity entered that second call: NCCL EP built in non-eager mode.
- A pipeline stage made only of dense layers has no such layer, so it skipped the reduction. The MoE stages waited in it while the dense stage moved on to the rerun.
- The result is a deadlock until the NCCL timeout, or a later WORLD collective pair

## Description

items.title: Start a chunked prefill only when its whole prompt fits
items.author: lmcafee-nvidia
items.summary: With chunked prefill enabled, the dynamic engine can stop making progress under KV-cache pressure, and never returns. lets a new request start a chunked prefill when the KV cache has room for one prompt token.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

With chunked prefill enabled, the dynamic engine can stop making progress
under KV-cache pressure, and `generate()` never returns.
`_can_schedule_chunked_prefill()` lets a new request start a chunked
prefill when the KV cache has room for one prompt token. A long prompt can
therefore start, take the last free blocks, and then wait for one more
block. A partial chunked prefill keeps its blocks until it finishes and is
never preempted. Requests decoding beside it then pause for want of a
block. If they hold no more blocks than the paused-block budget, nothing is
evicted

Breakable prefill CUDA graphs cannot be used for multimodal requests today: replaying the graph would drop the decoder's current inputs, such as the fused image embeddings and per-layer visual features (Qwen-VL DeepStack, Gemma 4 per-layer embeddings). These requests therefore run prefill eagerly.

### What does this PR do?

Starts all distillation teachers at once instead of one after another, which is what dominates startup when the recipe has many teachers.

`MultiTeacherModelManager` used to build one `TeacherModelManager` per teacher in a plain `for` loop, and each constructor blocked until that teacher's vLLM servers were fully up. With N teachers the wall clock was N x (engine init + CUDA graph capture). Teachers run on disjoint devices and share nothing, so this serialization was pure latency.

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores `torch.get_rng_state()`, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted run. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

items.body:
## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

How it happens:

- slime's colocated sender calls `update_weights_from_tensor` with `serialized_named_tensors`, `load_format="flattened_bucket"` and `weight_version`. It sets neither `selector` nor `disable_draft_model`.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

items.title: fix: run dense fused kernels through the FSDP2 LM head
items.author: ZiyiXu06
items.summary: Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads, including models such as Qwen3. Previously, the fused forward accessed directly, bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular Tensors with DTensors during matrix multipl…
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads,
including models such as Qwen3.

Previously, the fused forward accessed `lm_head.weight` directly,
bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular
Tensors with DTensors during matrix multiplication.

This change installs a fused LM head forward during backend initialization
and runs fused computation through `self.lm_head(...)`. It preserves
torch/liger backend selection and handles DTensor weights, device placement,
and hidden-state dtype inside the module boundary.

## Problem

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

```python
if not ground_truth:

### What does this PR do?

`ReplayBuffer._wait_for_next_poll()` sleeps a hard-coded `poll_interval=2.0` between TransferQueue metadata syncs (used
by both the sync `sample()` and the async `wait_for_sampleable()`). The trainer therefore notices the last finished
prompt up to 2 s late, and `timing_s/gen` is quantized to multiples of 2 s (main, vLLM: 2.21, 4.21, 4.21, 2.21 … s;
SGLang: 2.28 s every step). This PR replaces the sleep with a wait on a small completion counter that rollout workers
bump when a prompt reaches a terminal status. On 8x MI355X GSM8K GRPO it cuts `timing_s/gen` by 22–31%

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.

## Background

## Solution

- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

items.body:
## Problem

The fully-async worker receives a concurrency value derived from `sglang_server_concurrency`, which represents per-sample concurrency:

## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.

## Summary

Fixes the delta updater metrics initialization issue called out in https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/278#issuecomment-4904111448.

`UpdateWeightFromDistributedDelta._record_metrics()` writes density and wire-size counters to `self.update_weight_metrics`. This PR initializes that dictionary in `UpdateWeightFromDistributedDelta.__init__` so the first delta weight sync has metrics storage available.
